ranking_by: years in orbit, from launch of the first module to reentry (or to November 2026)
subject: space station
title: The 5 Longest-Lived Space Stations, Ranked (#1 Is Still Up)

scenes.text: Only two of these space stations are still flying. One is number one.
Number five: China's Tiangong. Its core module launched in 2021, so about five and a half years so far.
scenes.label: Tiangong · 5.5 years

scenes.text: Number four: Skylab, America's first station. Six years in orbit before it fell in 1979.
scenes.label: Skylab · 6 years

scenes.text: Number three: Salyut 7. Almost nine years before it came down in 1991.
scenes.label: Salyut 7 · ~9 years

scenes.text: Number two: Mir. Fifteen years, until it was steered into the Pacific in 2001.
scenes.label: Mir · 15 years

scenes.text: Number one: the International Space Station. First piece launched in 1998. Twenty-eight years, and still flying.
scenes.label: ISS · 28 years

description:
Time in orbit: ISS since 20 Nov 1998 (28 years in Nov 2026), Mir 19 Feb 1986 to 23 Mar 2001 (15 years), Salyut 7 19 Apr 1982 to 7 Feb 1991 (8.8 years), Skylab 14 May 1973 to 11 Jul 1979 (6.2 years), Tiangong since 29 Apr 2021 (5.6 years).
Salyut 6 (4.8 years) just misses the list.
Which station would you want to live on?
first_comment: Will Tiangong outlast the ISS? Tell us what we should rank next.
